slides.title: The Fairground
slides.text: The last workshop on the street is the Fairground, where every stall keeps a chart. A good chart answers a question before anyone asks it. A bad chart just stands there looking busy.

slides.title: Bars that speak
slides.text: Each bar's length is its count. Bananas sold 20, the longest bar on the chart. Read a bar by running your finger to the end of it, then down to its number. The scale tells you how much each step is worth.

visual.label: A bar graph of fruit sold at a stall: apples 12, bananas 20, pears 16; the longest bar makes 20

focus.cue: Apples: the bar stops at 12 on the scale.
Pears: 16 sold, between apples and bananas.

slides.title: Worked example: ribbons end to end
slides.text: Rough first: four short ribbons should make a bit more than a yard. Lay them on the line: a half, another half, then two quarters. The halves make a whole yard, and the quarters make another half.
steps: First ribbon: 1/2 yard, landing at the 1/2 mark
Second ribbon: 1/2 more, landing at 1 yard

visual.label: A number line from 0 to 2 yards with hops laying ribbons of 1/2, 1/2, 1/4 and 1/4 end to end, landing at 1 1/2

focus.cue: Lay the first ribbon: it reaches the 1/2 mark.
Two quarter ribbons in a row: another half yard.
The ribbons end at 1 1/2 yards in all.

slides.title: How many more?
slides.text: The question charts answer best is a comparison. Tuesday sold 20 lunches and Monday sold 12. How many more is a subtraction wearing a chart's clothes: 20 - 12 = 8. Always ask which two bars the question compares.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for the chart stalls.

words.means: facts collected by counting or measuring, before anyone charts them
what each step or picture on a graph is worth
a chart that shows counts as bars whose lengths you compare
a chart that stacks marks over a number line at each value

slides.title: Stretch: the sneaky scale
slides.text: Stretch: a picture graph uses one picture for every 5 points. A row shows 7 pictures. How many points is that, and why does the scale matter more than the pictures? Stretch work is never in the check.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Chart It and finish all 5 cases. Each case hands you a messy stall and asks for the chart that answers. Read the scale before you read any bar.
slides.alt: Data Detective, Chart It: a case's counts shown as a bar chart, the Bars view picked, a claim ready to pin.
